name: Sepehr Sarmadi Launch Review Checklist
author: Sepehr sarmadi

sections.description:
Sepehr Sarmadi Launch Review Checklist combines automated WordPress configuration checks with manual review for personal, corporate, and store sites. The dashboard shows the checks that block handoff and links to their cards. Reviewers can record outcomes and notes, run a full scan or selected quick rechecks, and export the current results as CSV or a print-friendly report. The interface supports English and Persian.

WooCommerce configuration checks are available when WooCommerce is active. The audit samples up to 200 recent published items, 250 recent images, the public homepage HTML, and up to eight internal links on the same origin. Test transactions, actual contact delivery, restore drills, external links, and specialist malware scans are manual reviews. A report reflects the checks and results available at the time of review.

Source Code

The package contains the original, readable PHP, JavaScript and CSS source in the plugin directory, includes/ and assets/. WordPress loads those files directly. No build step, bundled third-party JavaScript library or minified distribution is required.
sections.installation:
1. Install Sepehr Sarmadi Launch Review Checklist from Plugins > Add New or upload the ZIP using Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin and open Launch Review in the WordPress admin.
  3. Choose the project type in the plugin settings, run a scan, and review the results.
sections.faq:
Is WooCommerce required?

WooCommerce is optional. Its configuration checks run for store projects when it is active.

What data is saved?

The plugin stores its settings, the latest scan and quick rechecks, and manually entered notes and outcomes in the site’s WordPress database. If you select the delete-data option, uninstalling removes that data from the current site.

Does the plugin contact external services?

A scan requests the site’s own public homepage and samples same-origin links without sending WordPress session credentials or following redirects. External links are listed for manual review.

Google PageSpeed Insights is optional and disabled by default. If an administrator enables it and saves an API key, running a full scan sends the public homepage URL, the API key, and the mobile or desktop strategy to Google. The returned Lighthouse performance scores appear in the report. The API key is stored in WordPress settings, is not rendered back to the browser, and is not included in scan results or exports. An administrator can disable the service or remove the stored key from the plugin settings.

  • Google API Terms of Service
  • Google Privacy Policy
sections.changelog:
1.0.2

  • Resolve the WordPress sitemap index URL through the core sitemap API for plain and pretty permalinks.

1.0.1

  • Updated the plugin name and prefixes, preserved existing review data on upgrade, and enqueued the printable report assets.
  • Distributed the readable JavaScript and CSS source directly.

1.0

  • First stable release.
  • Isolated plugin code and styles, hardened scan requests and report output, and added an explicit PageSpeed opt-in.

0.3.3

  • Added a prioritized dashboard list of handoff blockers with direct checklist links, repair guidance for common issues, and targeted rechecks for homepage, indexing and WooCommerce checkout settings.

0.3.2

  • Record manual review outcomes and notes, retain them across rescans, and include them in dashboard readiness and exports.
  • Exclude not-applicable checks from scoring and allow untested nonessential checks without blocking readiness.

0.3.1

  • Renamed the final checklist section to Final checks.

0.3.0

  • Added personal, corporate and store checklists, WooCommerce configuration checks, homepage HTML and link sampling, and optional PageSpeed API scores.

0.2.10

  • Distinguish a hovered checklist tab from the selected section.

0.2.9

  • Give longer checklist labels more room in wide layouts and lighten the tab label weight.

0.2.8

  • Reduced the font size of checklist section tabs.

0.2.7

  • Redesigned the readiness overview and audit sections. Added per-section checklist filter counts and pressed states.

0.2.6

  • Refined the dashboard hierarchy, score display, navigation, and checklist cards in both theme-driven appearances.

0.2.5

  • Fit all seven checklist sections into one row when the checklist is wide enough and use a regular grid on smaller screens.

0.2.4

  • Follow the light or dark Global Styles background and prioritize the site’s actual link and button colors over decorative palette swatches.
  • Wrap checklist tabs so their underline and filters have separate space.

0.2.3

  • Automatically applies a contrast-adjusted accent from Global Styles, the theme Customizer, or the active Elementor kit. Color changes appear when the dashboard is next loaded.
  • Removed the manual appearance setting and improved the checklist tab underline.

0.2.2

  • Removed manual interface language selection. Interface and reports now follow the WordPress admin user locale automatically.
  • Kept automatic RTL for Persian and LTR for English.

0.2.0

  • Added Persian/English interface and report translation.
  • Added language setting: automatic from WordPress admin profile, Persian, or English.
  • Added left-to-right layout adjustments for English.
  • Translations are applied at presentation time so cached scan results remain language-independent.

0.1.0

  • Initial development preview.
